source: Paraphrased by the project team from the DSM-5-TR criteria structure; not APA text. Pending clinical verification.
label_footer: Hypothesis for clinician review; not a diagnosis.

conditions.label: Major depressive episode
conditions.icd10cm: Part of F32.x / F33.x / F31.x coding

elements.ask: Which depressive symptoms were present together, and was low mood or loss of interest among them?
Have these symptoms lasted at least two weeks?
elements.label: Duration ≥ 2 weeks

elements.ask: How have the symptoms affected work, study, relationships or self-care?
Any alcohol, drugs, new medication or medical illness (for example thyroid) that could explain the symptoms?
Has there been a recent bereavement or major loss? Clinical judgement applies.

differentials.label: Bipolar disorder
differentials.why: Depressive episodes also occur in bipolar disorder; ask about past high or irritable periods.

differentials.label: Persistent depressive disorder
differentials.why: Low mood for two years or more points to PDD as well as, or instead of, MDE.

differentials.label: Adjustment difficulties or expected response to loss
differentials.why: Low mood after a clear stressor may not reach episode thresholds.

elements.ask: Has there been a distinct period of unusually high or irritable mood with raised energy?
How long did that period last (at least a week), and was a hospital admission needed?
elements.label: Duration ≥ 1 week or hospitalised

elements.ask: During that period, which of the B-symptoms (grandiosity, less need for sleep, talkativeness, racing thoughts, distractibility, more activity, risky behaviour) were present?
Did that period cause marked problems at work or socially, need hospitalisation, or include psychotic symptoms?
Could a substance, medication or medical condition explain that period?

differentials.label: Hypomanic episode
differentials.why: A shorter or less severe period without marked impairment is hypomanic.

differentials.label: Substance- or medication-induced mood change
differentials.why: Stimulants, steroids or antidepressants can produce elevated periods.

elements.ask: Has there been a distinct period of unusually high or irritable mood with raised energy?
Did that period last at least four consecutive days?
elements.label: Duration ≥ 4 consecutive days

elements.ask: During that period, which of the B-symptoms were present?
Was the person clearly functioning differently from usual during that period?
Did other people notice the change?
Was the period severe enough for marked impairment, hospitalisation or psychotic symptoms? If so it is manic.
Could a substance, medication or medical condition explain that period?

differentials.label: Manic episode
differentials.why: Marked impairment, hospitalisation or psychotic features make the period manic.

differentials.label: Cyclothymic disorder
differentials.why: Repeated milder high periods over two years without full episodes.

elements.ask: Any history suggesting a psychotic disorder?
Has there ever been a period of unusually high or irritable mood with raised energy lasting several days?

differentials.label: Bipolar I or II disorder
differentials.why: Any past manic or hypomanic episode changes the diagnosis.

differentials.label: Persistent depressive disorder
differentials.why: Check whether low mood has lasted two years or more.

differentials.label: Generalized anxiety disorder
differentials.why: Worry, poor sleep, fatigue and poor concentration overlap with depression.

conditions.label: Bipolar I disorder
conditions.icd10cm: F31.x (by current or most recent episode, severity and remission)

elements.ask: Any history suggesting schizoaffective or another psychotic disorder?

differentials.label: Major depressive disorder
differentials.why: Without a manic episode, depressive episodes alone suggest MDD.

differentials.label: Substance-induced bipolar disorder
differentials.why: Rule out substances or medications as the cause of elevated periods.

elements.ask: Has there been both a hypomanic period and a major depressive episode?
Has any high period ever been severe enough to be manic?
Any history suggesting a psychotic disorder?
How have the depression or mood swings affected functioning?

differentials.label: Bipolar I disorder
differentials.why: Any manic episode makes it bipolar I.

differentials.label: Cyclothymic disorder
differentials.why: Milder periods that never meet full episode thresholds.

elements.ask: Over at least two years, have there been many milder high and low periods?
Were the symptoms present at least half the time, with no gap longer than two months?
Could a substance, medication or medical condition explain the mood changes?
How have the mood swings affected functioning?

differentials.label: Bipolar II disorder
differentials.why: A full hypomanic and a full depressive episode would point to bipolar II.

elements.ask: Has the low mood been present more days than not?
Has the low mood lasted at least two years?
elements.label: Duration ≥ 2 years

elements.ask: Which associated symptoms (appetite, sleep, energy, self-esteem, concentration, hopelessness) occur while depressed?
Over those two years, has there been any symptom-free stretch longer than two months?
Could a substance, medication or medical condition explain the low mood?
How has the long-standing low mood affected functioning?

differentials.label: Major depressive disorder
differentials.why: Full episodes within the two years are recorded as well.

elements.ask: Is the worry excessive and about several areas of life, on more days than not?
Has the worry been present for at least six months?
elements.label: Duration ≥ 6 months

elements.ask: Does the person find the worry hard to control?
Which associated symptoms (restlessness, fatigue, concentration, irritability, tension, sleep) come with the worry?
How does the worry affect work, study, relationships or daily life?
Any substance, medication or medical condition (for example thyroid) that could explain the anxiety?
Is the worry better explained by another disorder's focus, such as fear of judgement or panic attacks?

differentials.label: Social anxiety disorder
differentials.why: Worry focused on being judged by others points to SAD.

differentials.label: Panic disorder (not tracked)
differentials.why: Worry centred on panic attacks is better explained by panic disorder.

differentials.label: Depression with anxious distress
differentials.why: Anxiety confined to depressive episodes.

elements.ask: Is there fear or embarrassment about being watched or judged in social situations?
What does the person fear others will think or see?
Do these situations almost always cause fear?
Are the situations avoided, or endured with intense fear, because of that fear?
Is the fear out of proportion to the actual situation and context?
Has the fear lasted six months or more?
elements.label: Persistent ≥ 6 months

elements.ask: How does the social fear affect work, study or relationships?
Could a substance, medication or medical condition explain the fear?
Is it better explained by another disorder (for example panic disorder or autism)?
If a medical condition is present, is the fear unrelated to it or clearly excessive?

differentials.label: Agoraphobia (not tracked)
differentials.why: Fear of places where escape is hard, rather than of scrutiny.

differentials.label: Social withdrawal from low mood or low energy
differentials.why: Avoidance explained by depression is not social anxiety.

differentials.label: Panic disorder (not tracked)
differentials.why: Fear of having panic attacks in public.
